title: What is known about 1RB1LE_0RC0RB_1RD1RF_1LA0LE_0LD0LB_---0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LE_0RC0RB_1RD1RF_1LA0LE_0LD0LB_---0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

The right part of the tape is a chain of counters, each counting the carries of the one before: a base-3 stretch, a binary counter with 6-cell digits, and at the right end a base-3 odometer with 4-cell digits whose law is proved in Lean for every size. The rest of the tape, of copies of 110 separated by 0, 000 or 100, is not decoded.
verdict: The question is open. No halt in LONGRUN_STEPS steps of the C simulator; Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide), the run-length frame map for 106 frames, and the law of the odometer at the right end for every size.
Where a halt would come from. Only F0 halts and F is entered only from C reading 1 (1RF), millions of times (5,555,291 in 108 steps), always onto a 1.
What is missing. The left and middle part of the tape, and an invariant explaining why C never reads 1 with a 0 to its right.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The halting pattern never forms
claims.text: F is entered only from C reading 1 (1RF). In the first 108 steps that happens 5,555,291 times and F reads a 1 every time.

claims.title: The odometer at the right end, for every size
claims.text: Read the cells right of its low end four at a time, 0111 = 0, 0000 = 1, 0110 = 2. A visit in state B adds one in base 3 and always comes back out in state D. Blank tape is an endless row of digits 1, so a carry always stops. Proved from three token rows by induction on the number of digits.

claims.title: The frame map for 10<sup>6</sup> frames
claims.text: The run-length frame map of <code>bbtools.listframe</code> is defined for the first 10<sup>6</sup> frames from blank tape; if it is defined forever, the machine never halts (<code>no_halt_of_total</code>).

claims.title: The run uses the odometer law
claims.text: In the run, the cells right of 359 are entered only in state B, and all 51,723 of those visits up to step 10<sup>9</sup> (the first at step 367,121,349) are rows of the odometer law.

claims.title: A chain of counters
claims.text: The crossing profile at 10<sup>9</sup> steps: ×1/3 every 4 cells going right over 355 to 398 (the odometer), ×2 every 6 cells going right over 319 to 354, ×1/3 every 4 cells over 302 to 318; the cells -174 to 302 show no simple pattern.

claims.title: No halt in the first 30,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: The C simulator runs 30,000,000,000 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end cells -186 to 512 (699 cells), 302 ones.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.25·10<sup>8</sup> steps (accelerated run, blocks of 6)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/c/rleaccel.cpp (blocks of 6 cells, runs of a block crossed in one step, and cycle jumps, each used only after its one-cycle rule has been proved symbolically for all lengths above the minimums it needs; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 19,600,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt, in 10 seconds. That is more than 1.25·108 machine steps. It found no rule that repeats forever, so it does not decide the machine.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Needed: the rules of the left and middle part of the tape and of how they feed the chain on the right, then why C never reads 1 with a 0 to its right.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine builds a chain of counters at its right end, the last of them proved in Lean, fed by a part of the tape nobody has decoded yet. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the run-length accelerator (proved cycle jumps, blocks of 6).
No halt in the C simulator; 699 cells visited.
The base-3 counter at the right end, proved for every size.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Most of the tape is not decoded.

sections.heading: A chain of counters
html: The right part of the tape is a chain of counters, each counting the overflows of the one before it; the crossing profile, the number of times the head moves from each cell to the next one (c/cross.c, 109 steps, cells -174 to 398), shows them as stretches of constant ratio:

sections.heading: The odometer at the right end
html: The odometer (proved). Read the cells right of its low end four at a time: 0111 = 0, 0000 = 1, 0110 = 2 (lowest digit nearest the head). A visit in state B adds one in base 3: trailing 2s become 0s, the first other digit goes up by one, and the visit always comes back out in state D. Blank tape reads as 0000 0000 …, an endless row of digits 1, so a carry always stops and the odometer never overflows; it just gains a digit 2 at its top when a carry reaches the blank tape. lean/Odometer.lean proves this for every number of digits (o_carry, o_inc0, o_inc1, o_inc_blank) from three token rows (lean/VisitR.lean). In the run, the cells right of 359 are entered only in state B, and all 51,723 of those visits up to step 109 are these three rows, from step 367,121,349 on (c/vislaws.c). Each such visit comes from the binary stretch to its left, so the odometer counts the carries that leave that stretch.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: Where it could halt. Only F0 halts; F is entered only from C reading 1 (1RF), 5,555,291 times in the first 108 steps, always onto a 1 (then 0RD). Halting needs C to read 1 with a 0 to its right; that is a local pattern that the run avoids millions of times, but no CTL window up to 8 cells proves it.

sections.heading: What is left
html:
• The rest of the tape (cells -174 to 302 at 109): which counters it holds and how they feed the chain on the right.
  • Why C never reads 1 with a 0 to its right.

• Direct C simulation (c/longrun.c): 30,000,000,000 steps, no halt; at the end cells -186 to 512 (699 cells), 302 ones.
  • The frame map (py/frames.py, bbtools.listframe) is checked for 106 frames in Lean.
  • No macro-level accelerator.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.16).
After 109 steps the tape spans 576 cells (174 left of the start, 393 right), with a density of 1s of 0.488.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: chain of counters on the right
summary: A chain of counters on the right (the last one, a base-3 odometer with 4-cell digits, proved in Lean for every size) fed by an undecoded part; grows about 100 cells per tenfold time. Accelerated run: no halt in 1.25e8 steps.
